reviewer.name: Claude Sonnet, fresh subagent (cold reader 2)
reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-26 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session)

evidence: I read CONTEXT.txt whole first (the one-paragraph section “Inner child love”: the hand-on-heart and solar-plexus instruction, the quoted lines to the little one, “Make sure you are actually talking to your inner child, who is scared to death.”, then the fallback), then DRAFT.txt, SOURCE.txt and the_change. I formed my reading before opening ADMISSION.json and did not rely on its ledger (each evidence string there is a template that truncates the draft), so every row below is my own. I cannot see batch 479’s sample ch, so I checked the draft against the_change’s description of it. WHAT CHANGED: the words judged are “If you can’t do this in a loving way today, just put your hands there and see what you feel, no faking required.” Against the words it replaces (“…see what you feel. You don’t have to fake it!”) the first clause is word for word the same, and the separate exclamatory sentence becomes the tag “, no faking required”, which joins the fallback into one sentence. That is what the_change says: the no-warmth fallback, ending on his own words from his inner child guide (“Then rest your hands there and notice what you find, no faking required.”), with neither “You don’t have to fake it!” nor “Don’t fake it.” in it. CONTEXT holds the draft once and no leftover of the replaced sentence. MEANING AND FACTS: same condition (cannot do this lovingly today), same minimal act (hands there, notice what you feel), same release (no need to fake warmth). It stays a release and does not turn into a rule, so the published point (say it the way you would to a frightened child you actually love, no incantation) is kept. It adds no claim, fact, first-person detail or source (C01 to C04 absent); “this” still means saying the words to the little one in a loving way, and “there” the heart and solar plexus named earlier in the same paragraph. READING IT IN PLACE: no seam and no second voice. “who is scared to death” is the reason someone might not manage warmth on a given day, so the fallback arrives prepared (T03 absent). “in a loving way” coming back is a callback that fixes what “this” refers to, not an idle repeat, and “no faking required” appears once in the section (T26 absent here; I could not check the rest of the article from the files I was given). The tail is a plain dry tag in the paragraph’s blunt voice, built the way his guide builds it (fallback instruction, comma, “no faking required”). It also removes an echo: the old second sentence, “You don’t have to fake it!”, repeated the script’s “You don’t have to fix it.” in the same paragraph. The typographic apostrophe matches the context; no space before the full stop, no it’s/its slip, no quote marks around inner child. CLOSEST CALLS, judged not PRESENT: T22 coach register (it instructs and reassures, but the stance is real: do not perform love at a frightened child, and “today” and the dry tag come out of that thought rather than from reassurance alone); T10 generic permission (not the “you don’t have to X before Y” formula; the release answers the specific risk of faking warmth, in his published wording); T08 and T29 (the last sentence is a new consideration, a fallback, not a restatement of the paragraph, and without “no faking required” the one point the source insists on would be gone); T20 and T28 (this is the last sentence of the section as given, but it ends on the practice’s last step, not on a lesson, healing or summary; it is a 23-word sentence with a tag, not a short polished closer; the linter’s B7 did not fire; and the old separate exclamatory sentence was the more closer-like form); T21 (condition, act and release in one short sentence is an ordinary conditional, not coordinated argumentative jobs); T02 (a three-step practice paragraph, and the change turns two sentences into one). The writer’s T28 note (“not the end of its section”) does not match this CONTEXT.txt, where it is the last sentence, but my reading above is why I still find T28 absent. T01, T04 to T07, T09, T11 to T19, T23 to T25 and T27 absent. LINTER: “D9 follows the source order” is accepted: a one-sentence change inside a one-paragraph section, whose order is simply the order of doing the practice (hands, words, fallback); I checked T13 and T09 as the finding asks, and the paragraph does notice things (“who is scared to death”, “today”, the dry tag) and the draft is not weighted like its neighbours, so neither is present. “E36/E41 heavy second person” (13.0 per 100) is accepted: it counts three words (you, your, you) in 23, in an instruction where the reader is the one acting; it is one fallback step, not a run of coaching lines, and the sentence it replaces had four in 26 (about 15 per 100), so the change lowers it. No PRESENT row, both findings resolved, meaning kept, nothing added: PASS.
